arguments.summary: Fixed `split_row` in tinycsv/rows.py by replacing the naive `line.split(",")` + `strip('"')` with a small character-by-character state machine (no `csv` module). It tracks whether it is inside a quoted field: commas inside quotes are kept literal, a doubled `""` inside a quoted field becomes a single literal quote (advancing the index past both characters so the second quote isn't misread as the closing quote), and a quote only opens a field when it appears at the start of the field. Verified with the existing test suite (2 tests pass) plus manual checks: `split_row('a,"b,c",d')` → `['a', 'b,c', 'd']`, `split_row('"he said ""hi""",x')` → `['he said "hi"', 'x']`, and plain/empty-field cases behave as before.
